Map for pull request 3 (brief item 5: Safe passenger on by default, covering the drag and the landing). Line numbers refer to the read-only main copy at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rex-strength-lab/be83ea46-0fb6-5f45-86e4-061daa8f7429/scratchpad/main-tree/rex-strength-lab (main at 960fdfa). The scratch scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rex-strength-lab/be83ea46-0fb6-5f45-86e4-061daa8f7429/scratchpad/understand345/passenger/: table.js, onset.js, landing.js, catch.js, fixture.js, fixture2.js, blast.js, and engine-pr3.js, a scratch engine with the proposed edits.

**The brief's table, reproduced at 3,000 kg (person thrown 30 m at 45°, default dial).**
- With Safe passenger on: least disruptive is 3,342 kg-force, released at 16.4 m/s. The person lands at 18.0 m/s (like a 16.5 m fall).
- The ceiling is plaster from the landing: use 27,052 kg-force, onset 26,991 kg-force.
- With it off: 333 kg-force least, ceiling 334 kg-force (passenger).
- All four powers off with Safe passenger on: ceiling none (main gives passenger by drag at 39,700 kg-force). The all-out plaster reach is 1.36 m from the landing.
- Emulating PR2's recoil rule changes none of these, because the landing sets the shaking.

**Engine plan.** It is guarded, so with Safe passenger off every result keeps its exact value and keys.
1. Split `MOVES.throw.passenger` into `passengerLaunch` and `passengerDrag`, then define `passenger = !o.safePassenger && (launch || drag)`. With the switch off this gives exactly the same boolean as main.
2. Add `MOVES.throw.passengerLanding(r, o)`, returning `{absorbed: r.Eimpact, J: m·vImpact}` only when Safe passenger is on and the object is a passenger. This is the shimmer's source. It leaves throwOnce's result object untouched.
3. Proposed (not in the brief): drop the landing blast in throwBlast for a person with Safe passenger on, since its energy is taken back.
4. Keep `landShake` as it is. Keep Safe passenger out of `anyPower`.

**Fixture check.** On the scratch engine, exactly 8 powers-off fixture cases change: `plan|throw|person|inf|…|5`, which run with `safePassenger: true` in powers-off-cases.js. With a test-side shim that restores main's passenger rule, all 584 cases with a person or Safe passenger match the fixture, in both passes. The other cases have no passenger, so the new code doesn't run for them.

**Page plan.**
- `DEFAULTS.safePassenger: true`.
- Migration: an unmarked save loads with it on. I recommend bumping the marker to `saveV: 3`.
- Move the switch and rewrite its copy, and update `#powers-sum`.
- `passengerChip`/`passengerText`: covers the drag; new landing text for on and off.
- Effort box: credit `offBy.passenger`; replace the 'For a person…' line.
- `catchPassengerG`: check Safe passenger before the drag.
- Catch miss callout.
- Cards, README, and the research label for the drag fact.

**Tests.**
- powers.js: guard the 8 fixture keys; rewrite the 5a check at lines 94-97, which fails under the new rule; add a check of the landing split.
- presence.js line 238 turns round.
- shots.js: new checks for the default, the migration and the person-throw text. POWERS_OFF and the saveV expectations change.

**Overlap with PR2.** PR2 also edits these places:
- `MOVES.throw.shake`/`shakeFrom`, right beside the passenger rule.
- The comment above PASSENGER (engine.js line 4113).
- The sw-recoil label next to the Safe passenger switch.
- `offBy`/`OFF_NAME` (effort box lines 3627-3629).
- The bayThrow recoil lines.
- The Catch chips at 2808-2811 and duoFacts lines 4027-4028.
- Cards 15 and 20 in static-data.js. Each card is one line, so conflicts are likely.
- README line 5 and Known limits.

- data.js, if either regenerates it.

**PR4 and PR5.** PR4 later edits the same `#powers-sum`, DEFAULTS and intro hint, to add the Never knocked back switches. PR5 reads `passengerLanding`: at the least effort that is 14.6 kJ, between the 7.3 kJ floor and the 517 kJ flicker, so a faint flicker.

**The design that reproduces it.** When `cA.ownRecoil && !cB.immovable`, the charger is a body of unbounded mass:
1. Take the closing speed v (vRel).
2. Compute `h' = headOn(vToMomentum(v, mB), mB, Infinity)` and `contactForces(h', bB, bA, mB)`.
3. The one hit leaves at v (splat), or at c·tanh(2w) with w = asinh(u/c) (bounce). This is 2v/(1 + v²/c²), and its momentum is mB·c·sinh(2w) = 2γ²mBv.
4. The source supplies that momentum, plus what his footing hands the ground during the contact.
5. Q = h'.Q is the hit's energy, absorbed unless he means it.
6. Paradox where the one hit is held without limit. That is not something hb.H can tell you: holdOf gives Infinity for any bolted body, real rock too. The test is `holdsGround(cB) && (cB.anchor === 'bolted' || !horiz)`.
7. Light speed (pA = ∞) into a finite hold keeps main's 'unstoppable'.

brief_issues: Bolted on Unbreakable footing as 'held without limit' (brief item 4, Collide row) conflicts with main's own rules. (a) weakGround (engine.js:3533-3540) takes a bolted foot's sideways push whole: `capH = ... ownAnchor(ctx) === 'bolted' ? Infinity`, so the planet takes it and nothing is supplied. (b) The page's grid (app.html:3263) says 'Finite inertia (anything real, even bolted to the Earth)'. (c) Main gives light speed into bolted-on-unbreakable as 'unstoppable'/'planetMoves' (extra.js: ownRecoil off gives unstoppable planetMoves; calibration.js:368-369 checks the same on comic ground). An unbounded charger against Rex plus the Earth (finite mass) has a physical answer: the planet carried at his speed. Proposed decision: keep the brief's paradox, with a stated reason. Carrying the Earth at 18.1 m/s within the 0.314 m squash takes 3.1 × 10²⁷ N, 284 times the 1.1 × 10²⁵ N that holds the Earth's halves together (COL.F_HALVES). Read the weak-ground rule as extending to the planet: the ground can't bear that push, so the power supplies it without limit. Apply it only with the charger's ownRecoil on, keyed on holdsGround(cB). Relabel the grid column. Leave ownRecoil-off light speed as main's planetMoves, and record the asymmetry as a known limit. Below about 1.1 m/s the planet could bear the push; the lab ignores that edge.

'The charger's source supplies exactly the momentum the one hit gains' (brief item 4 Tests) holds only if the one hit's footing does nothing during the hit. Main counts that footing (toGround 'footing' = H·τ), and in a contest it is real. Prototype at 3,000 kg: the gain is 54,400 plus footing 612 = 55,000 kg·m/s at the default sprint (1.1%). From above on real ground at a 10^6.25 kg dial it is 217,000 + 13,200 (6%). Proposed: report carry.pGain and carry.footJ. Test the ledger (supplied = gain + toGround.J to 1e-9) rather than 'exactly the gain'. Cap the footing's force at the contact force (min(H, F)). Uncapped, the concrete under a landed-on Rex 'takes' 220,000 kg·m/s from a 13,000 kg·m/s hit.

The brief's figures are at 3,007 kg. At 3,000 kg: the source supplies 54,400 (not 54,600), the jump arrives at 286 m/s (not 287), and the splat frees 494 kJ (not 495). The 300 km/s splat is 8.99 × 10⁸ kg·m/s and 135 TJ; the bounce is 600 km/s and 1.80 × 10⁹ kg·m/s, as in the brief. runs.js's first '4 collide' block (toEndlessOcean = imm.h.el.pT) is the pre-Q13 reading. Its bounce figure is not the ground-frame momentum above low speed: at 50% c, 1.04 × 10¹² against the correct 2γ²mv = 1.20 × 10¹². Use the 'after Q13' block.

How long is the one hit 'carried along'? An unbounded charger never slows, so the carry lasts as long as he pushes, and the brief doesn't say. Proposed: the charger stops himself at the end of the squash (his own push, recoil to his source). The one hit then slides sideways from v (27.3 m at the default sprint splat; 102 m from 36.3 m/s in the bounce; 9.15 km from 300 km/s), or sinks from above. The 'slides past the nearest people' harm uses that slide. The default two-player least disruptive drops from 8,430 to 4,260 kg-force (bounce: 4,260 to 3,310).

From above on real ground (only when Unbreakable footing is off, e.g. the 'break the ground' preset), the existing sink model applied to Rex alone at the charger's speed drives him 1.8 cm into concrete at a 4.3 m/s landing (dial 10 t). 'The Truly immovable thought experiment stays as it is' contradicts 'a charger who takes his own recoil doesn't slow'. In it he stops dead or bounces, and the grid would put an unbounded charger against unlimited inertia in the ∞÷∞ cell. The steady push has the same clash: with ownRecoil and unlimited strength against an immovable body, main drives the pusher back ('pusherPlanet'/'pusherTorn'), which his own recoil forbids. PR 4 map for the shoving match, steady push, arm wrestle, shove, lift and throw of a partner, the fireball push, and the two Never knocked back switches. All runs used the main copy at 3,000 kg.
